commit-format: `<imperative description> ({profile})`: one clear, descriptive line, focused on what and why. The orchestrator's commits end with `(orchestrator)`.

lint.text:
Run ESLint with `--fix` on every JavaScript and TypeScript file the change adds or modifies since `{merge-base}`, committed or not, and confirm it reports no errors:

```sh
{ git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d {merge-base} -- '*.js' '*.mjs' '*.cjs' '*.jsx' '*.ts' '*.mts' '*.cts' '*.tsx'; git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- '*.js' '*.mjs' '*.cjs' '*.jsx' '*.ts' '*.mts' '*.cts' '*.tsx'; } | xargs -r npx eslint --fix
```

The reviewer runs it without `--fix`. Never lint the whole repository.

typecheck.text: Run `npm run typecheck` and confirm it passes.

tests.text: Run the tests relevant to the change with `npm test -- <paths>` (every test file the change adds or modifies, and the tests of the modules it changes) and confirm they pass.

knip.text: Run `npm run knip` and confirm it reports nothing.

light-and-dark.text: When the change affects UI or CSS, verify the result in a running app in both the light and the dark color scheme, and record what was checked in each.

agent-evals.text: When the change touches the Studio Code system prompt, a tool's definition, description, or result shape, or an agent skill or instruction, update the affected assertions in `scripts/eval/promptfoo.config.yaml` and run the affected cases with `npm run eval -- --filter-pattern "<case>"`. When `studio auth login` is unavailable, say so and flag the cases for a human eval run instead of skipping them silently.

agents-md.text: Follow `AGENTS.md` and the READMEs and design docs it points to for the areas the change touches, including its Common Pitfalls and its rule on code comments.

scope.text: Touch only the files the change requires; no unrelated refactors.

studio-ui.text: The `studio ui` browser app, serving this worktree's `apps/ui` and `apps/local`. From `{worktree}`, build it with `npm run cli:build:ui` (plain `cli:build` does not rebuild the UI), then start it with `DEV_CONFIG_DIR={studio-home} STUDIO_PROCESS_MANAGER_HOME={studio-home}/daemon node apps/cli/dist/cli/main.mjs ui --no-open --port <free port>`. The two variables keep it off the owner's `~/.studio` config and daemon; never start it without both. Port 8081 is the default and may be taken. Open `http://localhost:<port>` with a browser tool and dismiss the welcome tour; the app follows the system color scheme, so emulate `prefers-color-scheme` to check light and dark. Sites created from the app go to `~/Studio/`: name them starting with `{pipeline-slug}-` and delete each one you create. Before ending your turn, stop the server and run `site stop --all` as in `studio-cli`.

studio-cli.text: The `studio` CLI from this worktree. Build it with `npm run cli:build`, then run `DEV_CONFIG_DIR={studio-home} STUDIO_PROCESS_MANAGER_HOME={studio-home}/daemon node apps/cli/dist/cli/main.mjs <command>` from `{worktree}`, never without both variables, which keep it off the owner's `~/.studio` config and daemon. `--path` defaults to the current folder, so give every site command one: create sites with `site create --path {studio-home}/sites/<name> --skip-browser`, and delete them with `site delete <path> --no-files`. Before ending your turn, run `site stop --all`, which stops your own daemon and its sites.

ui-playground.text: `BROWSER=none npm -w @studio/ui run playground` renders real `apps/ui` components with sample data and no backend, in light and dark (`apps/ui/src/dev/README.md`); `BROWSER=none` keeps its `--open` from opening a browser. It serves on port 5300, or the next free port, which Vite prints. Stop it before ending your turn.

studio-web.text: Studio on the web: `npm -w @studio/ui run dev:static` serves `apps/ui` over its `static` connector, with sites in WordPress Playground, on port 3456 or the next free port, which Vite prints. Stop it before ending your turn.

evals.text: The Studio Code eval suite (`scripts/eval/README.md`): `npm run eval -- --filter-pattern "<case>"`, results with `npm run eval:view`. It needs `studio auth login` and consumes AI credits; each case uses its own temporary sites root. Run only the affected cases, one run at a time; the full suite (~25 minutes) only when the change touches the system prompt.

local-llm-servers.text: Local LLM servers to test against: Ollama (already installed), llama.cpp (`llama-server`), LM Studio and vLLM. The owner allows installing any of them that is missing, using them to test, and leaving them installed. Run your own instances on free ports with their data under `{studio-home}`; leave the owner's Ollama app on port 11434 and its `~/.ollama` folder alone. Download only very small models to test: free disk space is scarce. Keep RAM use low so the computer doesn't freeze. Stop every server you start before ending your turn.

demands.brief: Read the intent for what it demands: every outcome it asks for, and each input intended use produces that an outcome must handle.

omits.brief: Read the intent for what it leaves out: the cases, mechanisms, and guarantees it does not ask for and no intended use produces, and keep the spec to what remains.

owner-directions: No issue backs this pipeline: the owner chose to start it without one, with an intent of only its title and Goal.

The owner allows installing and using llama.cpp (llama-server), LM Studio and vLLM to test, and keeping them installed. Download only very small models to test, since disk space is scarce, and keep RAM use low so the computer does not freeze.
